This week's high heat, combined with untreated wastewater flows from Mexico in the Tijuana River Valley, have led to elevated hydrogen sulfide emissions, county officials said Friday.

The teams monitoring the South Bay found peaks as high as 4,500 ppb and up to an average of 2,100 ppb for one hour — peaking at night, when winds die down.
